title: AUO's Micro LED push signals a broader shift from displays to smart interfaces
content: AUO says its Micro LED technology is moving beyond screens and into a broader smart interface platform, even as one high-profile automotive project was shelved. The company argues that years of development, a growing production base, and expanding use cases have strengthened its position in a market still shaped by slow vehicle approvals and shifting electric vehicle strategies.

title: Toshiba cuts Kioxia stake as memory maker's valuation swings
content: Toshiba reduced its holding in Kioxia Holdings to 15.1% as of July 15, according to filings reported by Nikkei and Reuters. The change report, submitted to Japan's Kanto Local Finance Bureau on July 23, showed the Japanese conglomerate's stake had fallen from 16.1% in the previous filing on May 11.

title: Optical PD volume production lifts WIN Semiconductors' Q2 revenue 39% YoY
content: WIN Semiconductors, a gallium arsenide (GaAs) foundry, reported consolidated revenue of NT$5.26 billion (US$178 million) for the second quarter of 2026, up 14.5% sequentially and 39% year over year, driven by improved product mix, higher shipment volumes and the ramp-up of new products.

title: Alphabet's purchase commitments surge past US$800 billion amid AI infrastructure expansion
content: Alphabet disclosed in its latest quarterly filing that its purchase commitments and other contractual obligations had climbed to US$811 billion as of the end of June, underscoring the company's aggressive push to secure long-term AI infrastructure capacity.

title: KKR plans gradual exit as LCY Group accelerates semiconductor materials expansion
content: TSMC supplier LCY Group President Bowei Lee said private equity firm KKR & Co. plans to gradually divest its holdings in businesses affiliated with the Taiwanese chemical group, a move he believes will give the company greater flexibility to accelerate its expansion in semiconductor materials.

title: Lynas says Malaysia heavy rare earth project has gone over budget
content: Lynas Rare Earths said its heavy rare earth expansion in Malaysia has gone over budget as the Australia-based miner works to build out a non-China supply chain. The disclosure came alongside the latest quarterly results for the period ended June 30, 2026, in which revenue reached AU$289 million (US$202 million), up 70% year on year and the strongest level in four years.

title: Pantheon Electric expands copper platform as AI and grid demand tighten supply
content: Pantheon Electric said it has completed the acquisition of four manufacturers and built an integrated power infrastructure platform across 21 factories in North America and Europe. The company said the expansion came as AI data centers, grid upgrades, and US manufacturing drove stronger demand for copper-based infrastructure.

title: Google AI search reshapes traffic as publishers weigh blocking crawlers
content: Google's expansion of AI-driven search features is prompting a backlash from publishers and media companies that rely on search traffic. Over the past year, the company has rolled out AI Mode across search pages, using its Gemini chatbot to deliver direct answers that can keep users on Google instead of sending them to outside sites.

title: Airbus raises profit outlook as supply bottlenecks ease
content: Airbus updated its financial outlook for investors, saying easing supply-chain constraints should support stronger production and profit growth through 2029. According to Bloomberg, the European planemaker now expects adjusted annual operating profit of EUR12 billion-EUR13 billion (US$13.71 billion-US$14.84 billion) by 2029, nearly double current levels, and it plans a EUR5 billion (US$5.71 billion) share buyback over the next three years.

title: Trumpf's stabilizing sales point to a broader recovery in industrial demand
content: Trumpf said preliminary fiscal 2025/26 results showed its business stabilizing after several years of declines in orders and revenue. The German laser and smart manufacturing equipment maker reported slightly higher revenue and stronger-than-expected orders, suggesting demand may be recovering across its key markets and business lines.

title: PlayNitride bets on Tantium architecture, chip scaling to cut MicroLED costs 75% by 2030
content: Taiwan-based PlayNitride aims to reduce MicroLED production costs by 75% by 2030 through smaller chip designs and its proprietary high-efficiency Tantium chip architecture, positioning the technology for broader adoption across consumer electronics, automotive displays, AR devices, and optical interconnects, founder and chairman Charles Li said at South Korea's Display Business Forum 2026.

content: Qualcomm is expanding the reach of its Snapdragon platform across Samsung Electronics' Galaxy ecosystem, with Samsung's latest foldable smartphones, smartwatches and next-generation smart glasses all powered by Snapdragon processors. The move highlights the two companies' growing focus on on-device AI and seamless cross-device experiences.

title: Rapidus links 2nm chips, HBM and advanced packaging in AI foundry strategy
content: Rapidus is treating advanced packaging as a central part of its 2nm foundry strategy, not a downstream assembly service. The Japanese chipmaker aims to connect design enablement, front-end wafer processing, chiplet integration, packaging, testing and manufacturing data through its Innovative Integration for Manufacturing (IIM-1) model.
